question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x}{y}]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}{[\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}(\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{0}}{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2y}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2y}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{y} \\  & ={[\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}-1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2({e}^{2}-1)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
